articles.title: Taylor Swift Performs "Our Song" and "I Knew It, I Knew You" at the CMAs
articles.summary: The pop star, whose 'Toy Story 5' track marked a return to the country music world, is up for single of the year at the award show.

To kick off the performance, the global superstar started backstage as she danced past other country icons — including Brad Paisley, Little Big Town, Brooks & Dunn and Lainey Wilson — while singing her single from the Toy Story 5 soundtrack. She then grabbed her guitar and made her way onstage, where she was joined by Keith Urban on banjo.

Her CMAs appearance is the latest in a busy year for Swift, who was also inducted into the broader Songwriters Hall of Fame over the summer and is currently a front-runner in the Oscar race for best original song.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Performs 'I Knew It, I Knew You' and 'Our Song' Mashup at CMA Awards
articles.summary: "It's been a while," Taylor Swift sang during her performance of "I Knew It, I Knew You" at the Country Music Association Awards on Wednesday night — and it sure was, marking her first time performing at the show in 13 years. The singer gave the first public performance of "I Knew It, I Knew […]
articles.content:
"It's been a while," Taylor Swift sang during her performance of "I Knew It, I Knew You" at the Country Music Association Awards on Wednesday night — and it sure was, marking her first time performing at the show in 13 years.

The singer gave the first public performance of "I Knew It, I Knew You" about midway through the CMA Awards , bringing along a few famous friends for the ride. Swift began the performance backstage, singing the "Toy Story 5" song as she passed by country stars including Eric Church, Brad Paisley, Little Big Town, Brooks & Dunn, Sugarland and Lainey Wilson, the latter of whom was hosting the show. Swift was then brought to the CMA stage by Bill Anderson, the longest-serving member of the Grand Ole Opry, and finished "I Knew It, I Knew You" alongside Keith Urban, who played the "ganjo," or a banjo with six strings. Along with backup singers and a full band, Swift sang in front of a giant tree with a tire swing, weaving "Our Song" into "I Knew It, I Knew You" before finishing the song lying against the tree. (It's worth noting that "Our Song" was her first No. 1 at country, and "I Knew It, I Knew You" is her latest, honoring the 20-year gap between milestones.)

It was a welcome return to the CMA stage for Swift, who performed at the ceremony back in 2013 when she received the Pinnacle Award and sang "Red" with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss. She last appeared at the CMAs in 2016 as a surprise presenter to give Entertainer of the Year to Garth Brooks.

Her cameo at the show comes 20 years after her first appearance at the CMAs. Swift recently made a foray back into country with her "Toy Story 5" single "I Knew It, I Knew You," which was her first new song in over a decade to be marketed as a country song. articles.title: The Time Robert Pattinson Snuck Around Rikers Island (and Why It Could Help Him With James Bond)
articles.summary: Among the actor’s colorful roles is one rather surreal real-life moment in the hoosegow.
articles.content: Amid all the talk of whether Robert Pattinson ’s experiences will allow him to pull off a convincing James Bond , none feel as instructive as the time he went to prison. It was the middle of 2016, and Pattison didn’t commit any crimes, but he badly wanted to be seen as a someone who did. Pattinson was preparing for his role as Connie Nikas, a con on the run, in the Safdie Bros. jangly fugitive-drama Good Time . The Safdies knew some incarcerated people at Rikers, including their friend Buddy Duress, who would go on to be in the film. So, as Pattinson told a reporter writing about the movie in 2017, he begged Josh to get him into the facility. The director obliged, and while inside he and the future James Bond "just kind of went everywhere; we didn’t really ask for permission,” as Pattinson recalled at the time. (The interview was part of a story centered on walking around colorful parts of Queens with the Safdies, a tale in its own right.) The pair got deep inside the infamously locked-down institution, talking to wardens and inmates alike about life on the inside. One interaction in particular stuck with Pattinson. "I had gotten into all this makeup because I didn't want anyone I met in there to find out who I was or what I was doing; I wanted them to think I belonged. And I thought I was convincing. And then one of the inmates said to me, ‘What are you doing in here? Is it for a scared-straight program?' [The program to influence innocent-adrift teenagers.] I wasn’t convincing anyone." "I thought I was looking like some kind of tough guy but he could see right through me," he continued. (Pattinson is known for telling tall tales in interviews but this one is true — Josh Safdie confirmed the account.) On the one hand this unpersuasive cosplay can seem like one more reason the actor makes for an ill-fitting James Bond — you generally want your 007 to be a little more weathered than a pretty teenager, even ten years later (and also may validate all the skeptics who don’t like that this was kind of a corporate decision .) On the other hand, what’s more James Bond than sneaking around Rikers and getting out unscathed? A general MI6-ish resourcefulness marked Pattinson's time working with the Safdies. Hot off his Twilight run, Pattinson had reached out to the erstwhile collaborating brothers brothers simply after seeing a promotional photo for Daddy Longlegs , their gritty semi-autobiographical coming of age movie. He then read their script for what would become Uncut Gems and begged to be in that. The Safdies didn’t see Pattison in any of the top roles, including the lead middle-aged hustler played by Adam Sandler. But the filmmakers were so intrigued by his persistence that they decided to write a whole chase-drama for him — the movie that became Good Time . Sweet-talking your way into the confidence of a pair of powerful people so they'll do something for you they weren’t otherwise ready to do? M would be proud. articles.title: Netflix's Near-Perfect but Controversial New Supernatural Drama Series Is Dominating Streaming and Fans Are Demanding More
articles.summary: Courtesy of Netflix Many hit movies and TV shows have found their audience thanks to a strong word-of-mouth and reviews that just cannot be ignored. It looks like Netflix has tapped into one such series with their latest #1 sensation, and it is one that has brought as much controversy as success since its debut on November 11. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Many hit movies and TV shows have found their audience thanks to a strong word-of-mouth and reviews that just cannot be ignored. It looks like Netflix has tapped into one such series with their latest #1 sensation, and it is one that has brought as much controversy as success since its debut on November 11. Even before it aired an episode, The Body was picking up the kind of online headline-grabbing interest that would always pique the curiosity of subscribers and make them tune in when it finally dropped all of its eight episodes ready for binge-watching. That is exactly what subscribers have done, with the series generating 5.1 million views in its first week equating to over 37 million hours watched. Now The Body is the biggest show on Netflix in America and on the streamer's global chart proving that there is no better publicity than online controversy about the subjects of religion, supernatural rituals, and raunchy teen drama.

The Body is set around 20 years ago, following the members of St Mark's Catholic School's all-girl dance squad who find themselves falling under a strange influence after an initiation ceremony goes wrong and one of them ends up falling into a coma. Suddenly, the girls begin having delusions, unexpected and strange feelings, religious paranoia, and erratic changes in their behavior. The series stars Kristina Bogic, Genna Carling Meszaros, Jackson Kelly, and Sara Boustany as the main members of the group who are led though a journey of sexuality, superstition, faith and guilt in what creator Quinn Shephard calls, "a raunchy teen psychodrama with a dash of Catholic horror ." However, that is not what conservative advocacy group CitizenGO call it in their petition to have the series banned. Instead, they see it as a "blasphemous anti-Christian series featuring satanic ritual," and their petition has surpassed 100,000 signatures.

The subject of religion is one that often causes public outcry when mixed with stories of sexuality and violence. The Body has certainly managed to gain itself a reputation among Christian communities, even though Shephard is more than happy to defend the series against accusations that the series is a purposeful attack on religion. The creator said in several interviews prior to the show's release that she is more than happy for audiences to interpret the story however they want, and it is all ambiguous enough for there to be many interpretations out there. For Shephard, it is simply a story that is, in part, based on her own queer experiences of repression during her younger years. Whatever the truth behind it, for a show that has no big franchise behind it and no big name stars, The Body has made a huge impact that has left fans desperate for more.

The show's strong performance in its opening week could help it get the renewal that fans have been demanding since it debuted, but whether that happens is yet to be decided by Netflix. It is hard to see why a second season would not be given the go ahead. As well as its high viewership, the reviews are pretty much as good as they could be from the people that matter most - the audience. On Rotten Tomatoes' Tomatometer, critics have scored the show a healthy 90%, but the Popcornmeter is sitting on a near-perfect 97%. For a show that has brought with it a fair amount of controversy, it is a very impressive score, and one that could also go some way to giving Netflix the push needed to give the thumbs up to more.

Have you seen The Body ? Is the religious controversy justified, or is it just a TV show at the end of the day? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Inside James Bond 26’s Final 5 Screen Test & How Pattinson Stood Out Despite Amazon’s “Bias” Against Him
articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF A24 Having a major tech and media mogul choose the next 007 is almost, in itself, a plot right out of a James Bond film. The villain himself chooses Bond for promotion, to be a pawn in his game and make him more money? Throw in a loose nuke or rogue AI, and the script practically […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Having a major tech and media mogul choose the next 007 is almost, in itself, a plot right out of a James Bond film. The villain himself chooses Bond for promotion, to be a pawn in his game and make him more money? Throw in a loose nuke or rogue AI, and the script practically writes itself. Yet Jeff Bezos, who is (legally) not a supervillain, definitely had a hand in picking Robert Pattinson for the Bond role, and in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter , he reveals how it all went down. Weighing in on the final casting were Bezos, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman, and director Denis Villeneuve.

In the running for Bond were Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult, and Robert Pattinson, and Bezos admits they were actually biased against Pattinson because he was such a familiar movie star. "[H]e’s already so famous. We sort of thought, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown," says Bezos. "But in the screening tests, it was so obvious: He is James Bond."

For each of the five actors, Bezos revealed, they ran a full screen test, making them do three scenes apiece with full costumes and props. It hardly seems a surprise that a guy who has already handled action scenes in a hefty Batsuit could do likewise in a tuxedo, though Hoult has also done action in furry makeup for the X-Men movies. Being a charmer might have been more challenging — though Pattinson broke hearts in the Twilight saga, his Edward Cullen was something of a reluctant romantic in them. For a naturally good-looking guy, he gravitates towards weird and awkward characters, and Bond, the seducer supreme, is the opposite of that. Evidently, he erased any doubts, even pitted against more natural charmers like Hoult. It surely doesn't hurt that he just worked with Villeneuve on Dune .

Still, the Bond role is more than just about acting. It's a multi-year franchise commitment that takes precedence over any other project the star might want to do, and we can probably kiss his Batman goodbye once the current film is completed. Daniel Craig, after almost every shoot, would give interviews about how grueling it was and he didn't want to go right back to it . The days of Roger Moore using a stuntman and obvious rear-projection are long gone — now every actor in such a role has to try to be Tom Cruise and plausibly claim they did the stuff for real. If you're Denis Villeneuve, likely one and done with the franchise, of course you want the best available actor. Producers, however, need a long-term investment, and not another George Lazenby.

Will that be Pattinson? He showed his loyalty to Twilight even after it was obvious he didn't really understand the appeal of the films , or the tabloid gossip that surrounded his personal life, manufactured or otherwise. He has lived through being considered the most desirable movie star to women, and come out the other side. He gained tough guy cred in Tenet , and then The Batman . Everything about his track record would suggest he's up for it and qualified. All that remains is for us to see how he actually does.

articles.title: A SpongeBob Trading Card Celebrating Squidward's Most Infamous "Trash" Painting Just Sold for Nearly $60,000
articles.summary: The expression goes "one person's trash is another person's treasure," and that statement is especially true in the modern art world. Often times, art collectors spend ludicrous amounts of money on works that an ordinary person would stare at in bewilderment without a single thought regarding its meaning and, more importantly, how it could garner […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The expression goes "one person's trash is another person's treasure," and that statement is especially true in the modern art world. Often times, art collectors spend ludicrous amounts of money on works that an ordinary person would stare at in bewilderment without a single thought regarding its meaning and, more importantly, how it could garner such a high price tag. Some would see a Mark Rothko painting and feel blown away by its grandeur, while others would simply see red. Today, speculators and average joes alike can agree on one piece of art that sold for the right amount, as a rare Spongebob Squarepants trading card sold in an auction for an astounding $58, 560. Talk about a sweet victory!

This astronomical price for a single card is based on a throwaway gag from an older episode of the Nickelodeon animated series, one that centers on art and art collecting. The illustration on the collectible is a self-portrait of Squidward, which he titles "Bold and Brash." This parody of what many outsiders feel modern art looks like resembles a Dr. Seuss painting from his creepy "Secret Art ," with elongated features and single Eldritch eye in the frame. Will the value of this card be worth its investment from this auction, or did some wacky collector just create a holy grail out of a three-second joke? Let's dig into this auction oddity and solve this mystery.

Based on a brief moment from season two's episode "Artist Unknown" from 2001, the portrait card of Squidward Tentacles was part of Topps' Spongebob Squarepants 25th Anniversary set released earlier this year. With 200 cards in the base set, rare sketch cards and autographs were hidden in random packs that drove collectors to hunt down these hobby boxes in droves. These included Night Shift Manager variants, Bikini Bottom VIPs, Shadowboxes, Doodlebob Sketch Cards and Squidward's Gallery, which according to Topps' website showcased "how much Squidward loves Squidward."

The "Bold and Brash" card was one of those extremely limited inserts, with only 25 of them in existence scattered throughout the thousands of card boxes. Even more rare was the gold foil version— also known as a Superfractor — which was limited to a singular card across everything printed in this set. The odds of getting it were practically like winning a state lottery, but somehow, somebody found one and put it up for bidding during Goldin's November 14 auction. Even more shocking was how far one collector was willing to go to make sure this bizarre joke became a permanent part of their personal museum.

A true masterpiece 🖼️ From 2025 Topps Chrome SpongeBob, this 1-of-1 Superfractor of Squidward’s “Bold and Brash” self-portrait just sold for $58,560. pic.twitter.com/uBaMOxS3SS

"Bold and Brash" started with an asking price of $5000 on October 24, and the ensuing war of 27 bids rapidly jumped to the nearly 60K final number it reached on Nov. 14. The one-of-a-kind card, which was graded as a "near mint" 8 by the PSA, is officially the second highest sale from the popular set, only a few thousand dollars behind a gem mint red foil refractor card of Spongebob that sold for $61,610 in September. Only five copies of that particular card existed, but what made it more rare was that the winner of that auction received the only iteration of it to be graded by the PSA as a perfect ten.

In "Artist Unknown," Squidward is excited to teach art in a community rec center class until he discovers his only student is Spongebob. What Professor Tentacles wasn't prepared for was how much his annoying neighbor excels at every form of art known to man and sea creature, leading to him being kicked out of the class. Immediately following Spongebob's exile to the City Dump, art collector Monty P. Moneybags bursts into the classroom looking for art to buy. Among the pieces Squidward shows is this self-portrait, which the critic says “belongs in the trash,” moments before the center's janitor plucks it out of Squidward's tentacles and disposes of the piece in the rubbish bin. This gag quickly became a meme for fans of the shows just like handsome Squidward, but nobody thought it would be a joke worth tens of thousands of dollars.

At the end of the day, a collectible is only worth as much as somebody is willing to spend on it. Auctions only tell part of the story, and if a person is willing to go to the ends of the earth to acquire something, that item now has a new value. Nobody will dispute the rarity of this "Bold and Brash" card since it was limited to a serialization of one, but to value at it over $50K would seem bizarre to any outsider looking in. One could say the same about any modern art collection, but if one person's trash is another's treasure, then Squidward just cornered the market on highly collectible and valuable garbage.

Do you think this rare Squidward card will hold its value in 10 years, or will this rare item become a throwaway gag for another collector after it decreases in prices down the line? Join the conversation and let us know in the comments.

In Episode 3 of the season of Rings of Power that’s currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule , Gandalf has an interaction with the Secret Fire, where it’s revealed to him that five wizards were sent to save Middle-earth. That’s how we learned that Pallando, one of the two Blue Wizards, killed his partner, and it’s also when Gandalf learns that he’s been sent to save the corrupted Blue Wizard. When I asked co-creator Patrick McKay why they wanted to make the Dark Wizard Pallando, he began by saying:

While the end of Rings of Power Season 2 made me think the Dark Wizard was Saruman (even though that actually makes no sense timeline-wise), the other prevailing theory was that he was a Blue Wizard. Now, it’s confirmed that that’s the case, and McKay told me they made this decision because of how fascinating the lore is behind these two rather mysterious characters:

At one point, Tolkien wrote that the Blue Wizards could have been “founders or beginners of secret cults and magic traditions that outlasted the fall of Sauron” (via ScreenRant ). It’s not confirmed if this is used as inspiration for Rings of Power ; however, it does point to the potential moral ambiguity surrounding these magical beings.

Well, now I’m certainly excited to see where things go from here. I want to see Gandalf and Pallando interact more. I want to know if Gandalf can help his fellow wizard get away from the evil. And I want to know more about why the Blue Wizard killed his friend.

articles.content:
Blumhouse Atomic bosses Jason Blum and James Wan took a victory lap Wednesday at their Business of Fear panel, during which they discussed horror's banner year at the box office and why " Obsession " became the breakout hit of the summer.

But before the horror talk began, they had to address the name change. Blum's Blumhouse and Wan's Atomic Monster merged in 2024, and the combined labels were therefore known as Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Recently, in early November , Blumhouse Atomic Monster rebranded to just Blumhouse Atomic. Blum explained they rebranded to give a more definitive identity to the overarching banner of the two companies, while also clearing the way for both distinct labels to take credit for their work. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Skydance Plans Launch of Bundled Paramount+, HBO Max in Early 2027 Cineplex Boards Sanfic Title ‘La Residencia’ From ‘Algo Azul' Director Mariel García Spooner

Wan added that Blumhouse Atomic Monster was also "a bit of a mouthful."

"As Jason pointed out, it really still is Blumhouse movies and Atomic Monster movies," Wan added. "We're still making the movies as one company, but still under two labels. We put out a bunch of movies, and so we have to sort of divide it. Some movies play better at Atomic Monster, some movies play better at Blumhouse. At the start of movies, even though it's going to say Blumhouse Atomic Presents, our logos will still stand individually."

It was then on to horror's stellar year. Moderator Ray Subers, head of film at NRG, presented Blum and Wan with a stat that theater attendance for horror films in 2026 went up 7% from pre-pandemic levels, while attendance for all other genre films (action, sci-fi, rom-coms) decreased. Blum theorized this was because watching horror on the big screen is "participatory," and that audiences craved a "collective experience" after emerging from COVID lockdown. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I think that after COVID, audiences ran back to sporting events and ran back to concerts, but they had been fed movies," Blum said. "Kids had been fed movies so much at home that it took longer to discover and remember the movies [in the theater]. And I think horror specifically, if there's any genre that's close to a concert or a sporting event, I think horror is more than anything else because it's so participatory. I think movies generally, but horror specifically, are kind of joining sports and concerts as a great way to get out of your house and have a collective, fun, exciting thing to do that doesn't involve your phone."

The conversation then shifted to “Obsession.” Blum joined as an executive producer shortly after Focus Features acquired the film, which, from a budget of less than $1 million, grossed over $500 million worldwide. Blum said he thinks "Obsession" took off for two reasons. The first is because young people can relate to the "universal feeling" of being "obsessed or having someone obsessed with them." The second reason was that director Curry Barker sharpened his filmmaking skills on YouTube and social media before coming to Hollywood.

"I think that he has a dialogue with his audience, which he has honed over years and years and years of putting little pieces of content on YouTube and watching his audience react and adjusting to it," Blum said. "The best way I can describe it is it almost feels like when you're watching the movie, Curry is like whispering in your ear little funny things or like you're talking to this invisible hand that's directing the movie in a way that's very unique."

Wan added that the success of "Obsession" has inspired a whole new generation of filmmakers wanting to make scary movies, which reminds him of when he was trying to break into the industry with "Saw."

"That stigma is gone. Horror has crossed over from the black sheep of the household, right?” Wan said. "I really do credit the younger generation with accepting the genre in a big way and not turning your nose down on it in a snooty way. When I was doing 'Saw’ people looked down on it, right? And it was only a certain demographic that would come out and support the films that we made. But today, like today, it is cool and hip to be making horror films."

Dear SkyShowtime Employees, In September, we shared that SkyShowtime’s shareholders had initiated a review of strategic options, followed by the start of employee consultations in October. We are also grateful to Mark Neil, who has agreed to serve as Interim General Manager, overseeing the wind-down operating period. We are committed to supporting everyone at SkyShowtime throughout this process and sharing information as decisions are implemented. In the meantime, SkyShowtime continues to operate as normal for our members. Employee consultations remain ongoing in accordance with local requirements, and timing and process may vary by country. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the biggest features of Grand Theft Auto 6 is the ability to form a romantic relationship between protagonists Jason and Lucia, but keeping that connection together is easier said than done. You have to actively maintain the relationship throughout your adventure, as the game's story is often tied to how the characters interact with one another, whether it's on a platonic or intimate level. If you want to see the extent of new story content only accessible to a romantic playthrough, you have to employ a number of plans to keep your connection healthy rather than toxic.

There are four levels to the relationship mechanic in GTA 6 , through a hidden score that subtly changes as you go through multiple interactions between protagonists. No matter who you're playing as, you can affect your relationship through the activities you do, with more shared actions increasing the two characters' affinity for one another. However, you have to keep in mind the other character's interests and quirks, as catering to them can help you build your bond stronger than if you were just going through the motions.

It's easy to forget about communication with NPCs in any game, but GTA 6 is innovative in how it makes even the smallest details matter when it comes to who you interact with. Regardless of who you play, your partner (Jason for Lucia or Lucia for Jason) will check in on you throughout a given day, asking you to do various tasks or just seeing how you are. Ignoring these texts or calls is an easy way to tank your relationship fast, as every message left on read actively docks you down points. From the moment you start GTA 6 , your relationship could evolve in the following ways:

It doesn't matter if you initiate the communication or not, the important thing is you respond to what your partner says. For example, if they want to go on a date, it might be a good idea to do so rather than going off on your own to do something else. "Staying in touch" goes beyond just maintaining a digital presence with your partner, but also making sure they are involved with various aspects of your personal life. Holding their hand, going to bed at the same time, or just saying "Hi" can go a long way, but players have to make the effort organically rather than simply being responsive.

Sometimes, a straightforward compliment to your partner can advance your relationship, whether it's through a text, call, or in-person greeting. The worst way you can cause your connection to stumble is if you fail to respond to what your partner is saying, such as when they ask what you want to do. More often than not, GTA 6 will prompt you with options to "Go Out" when both Jason and Lucia are at home, letting you embrace different activities rather than just waiting for a phone call tied to the main story. Whenever you do one of the small interactions like texting or going out, a small heart above your partner's head will indicate you're on the right track.

At the same time, having a partner isn't just about frequent communication, but knowing when that communication matters. The best times to pursue an increase in relationship score is when a big story event concludes, or after a daring heist that had Lucia and Jason destroying property or fleeing cops. Laying low is a good thing when your wanted level is high, but life or death situations can also be a great place for bonding, or at least seeing how your partner wants to deal with the new intensity added to both of your lives. Sometimes, that could mean getting smaller tasks done, in other ways, it could be just being close to one another.

Instead of just sending a selfie to your partner, go to them physically and spend time interacting with them after something huge happens. This could be going out on an extravagant date after a heist nets you both a ton of money, such as visiting a club or doing an activity like scuba diving. In other cases, you could show up to them with some food to eat together, or take them for a romantic walk down the beach hand in hand. Checking in with a partner's mood to figure out what they want to do can clue you in to what activities will net you the strongest increase to the bond between both characters.

One of the easiest ways to mess up your partnership in GTA 6 is to go into the world without your significant other by your side. Although it's never clearly stated, going on solo heists and doing fun activities without your partner can actively hurt your relationship, especially if you're completing goals while actively ignoring their texts or calls. Without instigating conversations, your partner will feel left out, whether you're doing something legal or illegal. Robbing a gas station can put you at risk, and anger your partner when they want to protect or help you in that kind of dangerous situation.

Removed GTA 5 features makes your character feel less invincible in GTA 6 too, so that fear and anger at you robbing, killing, or otherwise causing mayhem is a much stronger feeling in Rockstar's juggernaut game. There are gameplay benefits to having your partner around in illegal activities too, not just by having another gun on your side, but smaller buffs you might not notice. In truth, leaving out your partner makes everything else harder, both in keeping your relationship healthy and actually trying to accomplish whatever pursuit you've set out for.

While you can take your partner to the beach, check in on them via text, and involve them in your illegal activities, some of the greatest shows of romance in GTA 6 come from what you're willing to sacrifice. In a gameplay sense, that means spending some money on keeping your relationship healthy, whether that's buying clothes for one another in a joint shopping trip or dropping cash on making your shared living space better. One of the first ways you can improve your relationship in Chapter 1 of GTA 6 is by simply spending money to paint the house or add new furniture through the resources you have.

If your partner expresses interest in doing a more expensive activity, spending the money on that task can be a way to exponentially raise the relationship "meter" hidden in GTA 6 . For players looking to go to Hot Together rank fast, this strategy might be the fastest, as long as they also remember to do the little things. If you drive to the zoo with your partner and don't open the car door for them, you are just going to end up with a neutral score in your overall relationship gain. The worst option here is to actively resist spending money, instead ignoring your partner's desires and wishes in another avoidant way.

Surprisingly, going to strip clubs as either protagonist actually doesn't reduce the relationship status you have, as both characters don't consider it "cheating." In fact, both Jason and Lucia make jokes about either character going to the club, with some circumstances actually allowing you to increase your bond by going to those raunchy locations together. Although the strip club is a quick way to lose the money you earn in GTA 6 , its explicit nature is a staple of the series players will inevitably looking for. As a result, Rockstar hasn't turned the strip club into a punishing area, and likely for the better.

Even returning to the strip club over and over doesn't seem to reduce relationship affinity in any way, but it could count as ignoring your partner if you spend more time at the club than at home. If you avoid doing errands or tending to your partner's needs by hanging out at the strip club, of course there will be repercussions. Thankfully though, Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game that provides many ways to correct your mistakes, so as long as you are consistent with keeping your partner happy, you'll find plenty of gameplay and narrative rewards for that work.

Will you be building a strong relationship in GTA 6 ? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Forget Jurassic Park, This Intense 99-Minute Dinosaur Thriller Is Roaring on Streaming After Flopping in Theaters
articles.summary: Courtesy of Warner Bros. If there is one type of movie guaranteed to draw in an audience, then it is usually one featuring dinosaurs. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If there is one type of movie guaranteed to draw in an audience, then it is usually one featuring dinosaurs. The prehistoric creatures have been fascinating people for more than a hundred years, and have appeared on screen in every era of cinema. From stop-motion appearances in movies like King Kong and 65 Million Years BC , to modern CGI iterations, there is something still awesome about seeing dinosaurs come to life on screen. Yet this year's big dino flick starring Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor couldn't take a bite out of the box office despite being rated higher than most of the mighty Jurassic Park franchise . Now, though The End of Oak Street is finally roaring with its debut on streaming, as it charged straight to the top of the HBO Max global chart this week. Once again it is a sign that box office performance is becoming less relevant when many are happy to wait a little longer to catch non-franchise movies in their own homes.

The End of Oak Street has everything you would expect from a summer blockbuster. Big star names in Hathaway and McGregor, J.J. Abrams producing, and It Follows helmer David Robert Mitchell writing and directing. The film is set in 1982, when novelist Denise (Hathaway) and her pizza-delivery man husband, Greg (McGregor) find their neighborhood being transported back 65 million years into the past where the residents need to work together in order to survive a dangerous new world of predators that are almost inescapable. Yet just like Adam Driver's sci-fi dinosaur movie 65 , The End of Oak Street just could not capture an audience when it was released right in the middle of the summer season on August 14. Instead, it has had to wait three months to finally prove that it did have an audience out there waiting for it after all.

The ambition behind The End of Oak Street was clear to see from the movie's trailers, with the special effects easily matching those of recent Jurassic World movies and a very positive initial reaction from critics . The Tomatometer maintained a high 86% score from critics, who praised it as a thrilling "pulpy good fun" film that should be perfect for the millions who have turned almost every Jurassic World movie into a $1 billion success. Even audiences were mostly positive as its 76% score suggested, yet they just did not turn out in numbers during its theatrical run. With a budget of around $80-90 million, the worldwide gross of $122 million made it a big flop during a summer filled with surprising low-budget hits like Obsession and Resident Evil.

Now, just like so many movies, The End of Oak Street has become the latest release to find redemption as a huge streaming hit. The movie has plenty to offer a streaming audience. It has action, adventure, fits with a family viewing scenario, some great special effects, and a brisk 99-minute running time meaning it will not take up hours like many movies tend to these days. The film also plays well into the one thing that fans wanted more of in Jurassic World: Dominion ; dinosaurs roaming around the streets of a neighborhood picking off people one by one without mercy. Considering the number of complaints that Jurassic World movie received for not delivering what audiences wanted, it is even more surprising that The End of Oak Street did perform better. With streaming performance now being almost as important as theatrical, it seems that judging whether a movie is a success is something that can only be done after it has a chance to prove itself at home.

Have you seen The End of Oak Street ? Should it have been a hit in cinemas? Let us know in the comments.

Another lesser-remembered blaze from last year was the Sunset Fire . It broke out near Runyon Canyon in the Hollywood Hills and scorched about 43 acres before firefighters gained the upper hand. The intervening days will see a march upward toward that high-water mark.

articles.title: Bryan Freedman Sued Over Hush-Money Deals Shielding Michael Jackson Estate
articles.summary: The Cascio siblings claim the attorney had a conflict of interest when he brokered their settlements with the singer's estate.
articles.content:
Five siblings at the forefront of sexual assault allegations against Michael Jackson have sued Bryan Freedman , Hollywood's favorite lawyer who was allegedly enlisted by the pop star's estate to deceive them into signing hush-money deals.

In a lawsuit filed on Wednesday in California state court, Frank Cascio and his siblings Edward, Dominic, Aldo and Marie-Nicole accuse Freedman of legal malpractice, breach of fiduciary duty and fraud. They allege that he duped them into signing agreements barring them from publicly discussing Jackson's alleged abuse that have emerged as obstacles in ongoing litigation against the estate, which Freedman allegedly worked for while representing the siblings when the deals were signed in 2019.

The siblings' relationship with Freedman started five years earlier when a lawsuit was filed against Edward, who at the time was defending the singer from sexual abuse allegations, and the estate in connection to his work on a posthumous Jackson album. At the recommendation of the estate, which paid for legal fees, he retained Freedman, according to the complaint.

The lawsuit says Jackson's estate again turned to Freedman to broker deals with the Cascio siblings in the wake of Leaving Neverland , which featured sexual abuse allegations against the singer. Freedman told the siblings that they didn't need to hire their own lawyer and that the settlement was fair and nonnegotiable, according to the complaint.

"None of this was true," writes Howard King, a lawyer for the siblings, in the filing. "At the time, Freedman represented the estate, including in connection with litigation against HBO, which had broadcast Leaving Neverland ."

The document the estate presented framed the settlement as an "acquisition and consulting agreement," identifying the deal as a purchase of the family's life story rights, the lawsuit says. Under the terms of the contract, the estate made five annual payments of $690,000 to each sibling. In exchange, they are barred from publicly discussing Jackson's alleged sexual abuse and subject to mandatory arbitration provisions, among other things that include releasing the estate and its representatives from potential liability. It requires the entire family to return all payments if one member is violates the terms of the deal, according to the complaint.

The siblings say they learned of Freedman's alleged conflict of interest when the lawyer in 2024 told them that the estate hadn't paid enough money five years earlier. He allegedly called the deal "toilet paper" and that he "had enough on the estate" that would convince its representatives to "do right" by them, the lawsuit says. After Freedman instructed the siblings to hire him, they retained another lawyer, who told the estate that the 2019 deals would be challenged. The estate later filed an arbitration demand against the siblings for breaching the nondisparagement and confidentiality provisions of their deal.

"If Freedman had not fraudulently induced Plaintiffs into signing the agreement, they never would have been dragged into litigation for publicly discussing Jackson's abuse," states the complaint, which notes that a child sex trafficking lawsuit they had filed against the estate was forced into arbitration under the terms of the 2019 agreement.

The lawsuit was filed as Freedman, who didn't respond to a request for comment, fields accusations of helping orchestrate online smear campaigns in public relations battles against his clients' adversaries. A trial is scheduled to start next year involving Rebel Wilson and producer Amanda Ghost, who accuses the actress and her public relations team of creating a site that accused Ghost of sex trafficking.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The latest update on Netflix's Solo Leveling live-action adaptation hints at perfecting one role that the original series didn't. Solo Leveling is a power fantasy series focused on a man who aims to become the best version of himself, acquiring wealth and power for himself and his family. The series perfectly captures this through its first two anime seasons, faithfully adapting the manhwa source material and showing Sung Jinwoo leveling up at every turn. However, considering the series revolves around a man acquiring immense power, it leaves little room for the development of other characters. While several characters still get their moments in the spotlight, particularly the male characters, the series has also been criticized for its lack of compelling female characters.

This isn't necessarily a problem with Solo Leveling itself, but rather with the power fantasy genre, which often incorporates other characters, especially female characters, merely to amplify the presence of the male lead. Solo Leveling does this as well, particularly with Cha Hae-in, a character with immense potential. As the only female S-Rank Hunter in the entire nation, her position is one that should have received greater attention, yet both the anime and manhwa largely overlook it. However, Netflix's Solo Leveling has been hinting at adapting this character differently, and the latest update from the actress set to play Cha Hae-in suggests that her role will be expanded and improved in several ways.

Han So-hee's casting as Cha Hae-in was one of the earliest confirmations for Netflix's Solo Leveling live-action adaptation, and one of the most intriguing details about this adaptation was the revelation that the project would follow the K-drama format. This led many fans to speculate that the series might also lean more heavily into romance, something some fans already suspected given Cha Hae-in's early casting confirmation. Now, a new interview with the actress, featured in ELLE Korea's December 2026 issue , has revealed how she is approaching the character with dedication. Han So-hee revealed that since filming is still underway, she is still getting to know the character. However, the actress also explained that she understands the character's vulnerability.

Her explanation reveals that even though Cha Hae-in is the only female S-Rank Hunter , she still has a vulnerability rooted in her humanity. The actress explained that she approaches filming with the understanding that Cha Hae-in is someone who fights to protect others and lives for the moments when others are happy. Her approach to the character highlights how Netflix may be focusing more on her, giving her the opportunity to define her own character. It could also aim to highlight how and why Cha Hae-in became the only S-Rank Hunter in the entire nation, adding the depth that both the anime and the original source material lacked.

Considering how K-dramas tend to place particular emphasis on emotional expression, giving Cha Hae-in more emotional sequences and developing her romance with Jinwoo rather than keeping it as a background element could add more depth to the Solo Leveling series. This would not only address the lack of female character development that the anime has been criticized for, despite having a strong candidate, but also introduce more depth to Solo Leveling itself, addressing complaints that its story feels bland and relies too heavily on action.

The story of a high school soccer team that gets stranded in the woods, and the mystery of the savagery and evil forces that followed them into adulthood years […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Yellowjackets has been one of the biggest cult-hit TV shows of the last few years and has rightfully earned the title of being the "next Lost." The story of a high school soccer team that gets stranded in the woods, and the mystery of the savagery and evil forces that followed them into adulthood years later, will finally be brought to a close when Season 4 premieres this week. And like so many high-concept genre series, everything is riding on how the showrunners land the plane in this final season.

ComicBook.com's Chris Killian had a chance to sit down with the cast and creators of Yellowjackets and talk about crafting the show's ending. Showrunners Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson had some interesting things to say about when they knew they had the ending they wanted, and the difference between knowing what that ending is, and actually getting to it over the course of the show, without deviating course.

Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson were candid in their explanation of how Yellowjackets has taken a winding path to its ending. As the pair describes below, even though they may have discovered an overarching plan for the ending early on, it was very hard to keep it in clear sight at times, once they got into the finer details of the series and its character arcs.

"I mean, we always had the end sort of concept in mind. Yeah. And then, to some extent, for a while it was just a question of, 'Is that actually where we're going? Is that going to change more substantially than we think?'" Lyle explained. "And then, at a certain point, as we were kind of hitting the big story beats that we had planned… As we were hitting those, we were like, 'Oh, I think we are still on the same path.' And so a lot of the smaller details and the ways that we decided to get there have changed. But it was more of a discovery that we were, in fact, on the path that we thought we were on, if that makes sense."

"Yeah. Absolutely," Nickerson said in agreement. "The only thing that I would add to that is that is completely true. But I think that a story is ultimately so much more than a collection of plot points. And we will spend hours discussing the inflection line because it can change. Like what it means, or how it lands, or what it touches on. So there was a lot of discovery throughout the entire thing. And even in the writing of the last script, there were very important creative decisions made in terms of the totality of the piece… Meaning gets added to it all the time, even if specific plot points aren't changing."

The pair go deeper into some of the character arcs that changed during the course of the show. Check out their full explanation in the video above! Yellowjackets : The Final Season premieres on Showtime (and Paramount+) on November 20th.

articles.title: One of Batman's Most Memorable Movie Moments Started With This Miniature Batwing (& It Could Be Yours For a Bruce Wayne Worthy Price)
articles.summary: Courtesy of Warner Bros. In 1989, Tim Burton brought Batman to cinemas for the first time ever in a dark and gothic take of the Caped Crusader and now fans can get their hands on a piece of the movie's production that created a moment that has become one of the film's most iconic images. As part of Heritage […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In 1989, Tim Burton brought Batman to cinemas for the first time ever in a dark and gothic take of the Caped Crusader and now fans can get their hands on a piece of the movie's production that created a moment that has become one of the film's most iconic images. As part of Heritage Auctions' Hollywood and Entertainment Signature Auction , among the many pieces of movie memorabilia on sale is a miniature Batwing that was used during the production of Batman in several moments in the final act, including the unforgettable image where Michael Keaton's Dark Knight flies it in front of the moon, perfectly recreating the Bat Symbol in the sky. In a movie filled with scenes that have continued to be quoted and live on across the decades, this is right up there with the best of them.

37 years since Batman swooped into cinemas, the miniature model that was used to make this scene and other Batwing moments when Keaton's superhero faces Jack Nicholson's Joker on the streets of Gotham City is now available to be purchased by anyone with pockets deep enough to afford it. Obviously, any prop from a movie as iconic as Batman does not come cheap and long before the hammer falls on this auction the price has already hit $35,000. What do you get for your money other than a piece of movie history? A 27-inch fiberglass, resin and acrylic model with working wing-tips, LED lights, a detailed internal flight panel, and a hand-painted figure of Keaton's Batman in the cockpit. As a piece that was used during the filming of the movie, it does have the usual production-used signs of wear, but that is not something that will concern serious collectors in this case.

Before Batman opened in cinemas in 1989 , the caped crusader had been confined to TV, most notably with the face of Adam West in the 1960s series and TV movie. The idea of superheroes being big business and in some cases being possible to do in a live-action feature was one that many balked at four decades ago. Movies relied on practical effects, meaning that comic book characters with big fantasy locations linked to them were almost impossible to make, and though Batman did not have this against him, superheros were not a priority for studios. Burton's Batman was therefore one of the most impressive and groundbreaking movies of the 1980s, ushering in a new era of superhero movies that built on the previous success of Christopher Reeve's early Superman movies and other low-level success stories like Swamp Thing . That meant future Batman movies had a lot to live up to.

Keaton's second outing as the Dark Knight in Batman Returns proved to be a hint of just how quickly the tide can turn against a character, as many slammed the movie for being too dark and mature , even though it was never really made with children in mind. This saw the next Batman movies replace Burton's gothic sensibilities with bright-colored villains and more humor, which killed off the franchise for several years until Christopher Nolan delivered what still stands as the best run of Batman movies ever. This grounded take starring Christian Bale brought comic books into an era where every superhero needed to be gritty and based more in reality. In recent years, this had changed again, with Matt Reeves' The Batman going right back to the character's detective roots and stripping away all fantasy elements entirely to great success. Wherever Batman goes next, there will always be those who want to return to the older iterations, right now, auctions like the Batwing sale is one of the best ways of keeping that old flame alive.

Which is your favorite iteration of Batman? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 3 More Cult Sci-Fi Movies That Were Too Weird For Mainstream Audiences, Including A Controversial Dystopian Comedy

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google By its very definition, the scope of the sci-fi genre is incredibly broad. Anything that takes vaguely scientific ideas and uses them to weave a fictional narrative can be considered science fiction, and that has led to some pretty out-there stories over the years. Many of the best sci-fi movies are those that cleverly employ established tropes, giving audiences an entertaining experience that feels very much in line with their expectations of the genre. However, there are also always movies that test the boundaries, pushing their sci-fi narratives in strange and sometimes unexpected directions.

Recently, we took a look at some cult sci-fi movies too weird for mainstream audiences , but it turns out that the genre has many more. The following films were all pretty odd and struggled to find major, widespread success, but they have come to be remembered fondly on a smaller scale. Each of these sci-fi movies has its own cult following, even though they proved to be just a little too bizarre for a more generalized audience.

Following the success of Donnie Darko , Richard Kelly attempted to bring a different kind of complex narrative to life on the big screen. 2006's Southland Tales was an incredibly ambitious film, combining the talents of many big-name actors. The controversial dystopian comedy follows the story of various characters in an alternate near-future Los Angeles shortly after the outbreak of World War III. Now remembered as a cult sci-fi flop , Southland Tales polarized critics and struggled to secure any sort of major audience, simply because its ideas were incredibly out-there. Dwayne Johnson's portrayal of an amnesiac action star, the bizarre musical and dance numbers, and the inclusion of a rift in the space-time continuum all combine to make Southland Tales just a few steps beyond what general audiences are able to tolerate from a sci-fi movie. However, despite the film's lack of commercial success, it secured a loyal cult following who appreciate its uniquely bizarre mythology, and Southland Tales remains an underrated cult classic two decades after its release.

Despite technically being a sci-fi movie based on a Stephen King story , 1992's The Lawnmower Man took so many liberties with the source material that the famed author sued to have his name removed from all marketing. The film's story involves a scientist enhancing a man with developmental difficulties, using virtual reality and drugs to vastly increase his intellect. The film's blend of cyberpunk, techno-thriller, and psychological horror made for a pretty odd mix, especially as it was released at a time when audiences had little experience with even one of those sci-fi tropes, let alone all at once. The result was The Lawnmower Man being unable to secure any sort of widespread success, largely because both critics and audiences felt it was, all in all, a very weird movie. That didn't stop it from becoming a cult classic, though, with its early use of CGI technology and ambitious technological horror celebrated by its relatively small contingent of fans. Despite its many odd qualities, The Lawnmower Man remains a '90s cult classic, as well as an oft-forgotten chapter in sci-fi history.

The career of Tim Burton has seen the director deliver many hugely successful blockbusters, but Mars Attacks! isn't often named among them. The 1996 sci-fi movie is considered a cult classic , but it struggled to achieve mainstream success upon its initial release. The movie's central premise — aliens from Mars invading Earth — evokes timeless sci-fi ideas, but the execution was far from what many expected of Mars Attacks! . Approaching the whole premise as a B-movie realized with some of the best visual effects available at the time, and then offsetting its science fiction with slapstick comedy and deliberately cartoonish violence was, simply put, not what anyone expected. The air of deliberate tackiness proved off-putting to many, denying Mars Attacks! the mainstream success it really deserved. However, the movie quickly secured a cult following and has, in the decades since, been celebrated as an underrated sci-fi classic, outlining that just because a movie struggles to impress mainstream audiences, that doesn't mean it should be easily written off.

articles.title: 5 Comic Sidekicks Who Outclass Their Mentors (Even If They Don't Look the Part)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Sidekicks have been an important part of adventures stories for millennia, so when DC Comics introduced Robin in 1940, it was just more fully embracing the mythological roots of the superhero. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Sidekicks have been an important part of adventures stories for millennia, so when DC Comics introduced Robin in 1940, it was just more fully embracing the mythological roots of the superhero. Since then, DC and Marvel Comics have created a variety of sidekicks, with some of the most popular ever often starting out as junior partners to the world's greatest heroes. Sidekicks are all about potential; their mentors train them so they can join the fight against evil, passing on what they've learned to the next generation. Often times, sidekicks are on the same power/skill level of their mentors, mostly because it makes it easier for them to train.

However, there have been times when heroes chose a sidekick who ended up outclassing them. These sidekicks sometimes had training before they started or tapped into greater sources of power as time went on. Other times, the heroes recruit a more powerful sidekick to help train them. While we all can name sidekicks that obviously outclass their mentors, there are others who don't look the part, which makes it all the more surprising. These five comic sidekicks are more powerful than the heroes training them, but you'd never know it by looking at them.

Bart Allen was introduced during Mark Waid's '90s run on The Flash . He was meant to be the new speedster sidekick, but the character made a pretty big splash right away, and was moved over to his own book. Bart is the grandson of Barry Allen from the 31st century (Barry went to the future after "The Trial of Barry Allen", where Iris was, and they started a family, birthing the Tornado Twins before Barry died in Crisis ), born with the Speed Force and raised in virtual reality. He was the ultimate ADHD kid.

Bart wasn't Kid Flash, though , at least not back then. He wasn't the Flash's sidekick. Instead, he was being trained by two of the oldest speedsters on the planet – Jay Garrick, who he was living with in Keystone City, and Max Mercury, the Zen speedster who had posited the existence of the Speed Force years before it was discovered. While Jay and Max are both potent heroes, they're more skilled than powerful. Bart's connection to the Speed Force was much more powerful than theirs, allowing him to outpace his mentors when he really turned on the power.

Damian Wayne is the son of Batman and Talia al Ghul, the heir to the Demon's Head and the mantle of the Dark Knight. He was introduced in the classic "Batman and Son", a story that seemingly ended with his death. However, it was only the beginning for young Damian. He'd stay in the shadows until his father's "death" in Final Crisis , when he tried to step up as the heir of the Bat. However, he was 12, which meant that he was more suited for another Bat-mantle – that of Robin. Damian ended up becoming the Boy Wonder when Dick Grayson took over as Batman, with the two of them forming a different Dynamic Duo.

Damian was trained almost from birth by his mother to be better than both his grandfather and father. I think saying that Damian is better than Bruce might be a stretch – although he probably has the potential to be – however, he was more skilled than his first mentor, Dick. Grayson is one of the best superheroes out there, but Damian was his superior in numerous ways. Dick knew it too, and treated Damian with respect, helping him become a a better person and hero.

Once upon a time, Aquaman needed a sidekick. Instead of calling him Aquaboy, which isn't great but not that bad, they decided to go another direction and Aqualad was born. That name was terrible – made worse by the fact that his real name was Garth – and he'd become one of the least popular DC sidekicks of them all. He couldn't even get onto the New Teen Titans and he was one of the founding members of the original group. The death of Aquagirl during Crisis left him adrift and he faded away with the rest of the Aquaman mythos in the late '80s. However, Peter David's brilliant Aquaman (Vol. 4) salvaged the character , with Garth getting a chance to reach his highest potential.

Atlantis was once the home of humanity's magic back before it sank, so Atlanteans mages are especially powerful. It was eventually revealed that Garth was a powerful magic user and he ended up becoming Tempest (go look up his red and black costume at the time – he looked amazing). While Arthur's aqua-telepathy and superhuman physicality made him powerful, Tempest's magic gave him the greater potential. Of course, since Arthur has connected to the Blue, he's certainly more powerful than Garth, but there was a long time that Tempest was more powerful than Aquaman.

Cassandra Cain is the daughter of two of the greatest assassins of them all, David Cain and Lady Shiva. She was trained to enter the family business and Cain went to some extremes to make his daughter deadly. He wouldn't speak at all around her, forcing her to learn to read body language to figure out what people wanted or were going to do next. This made her amazing martial artist, allowing her to predict her foes' move and use the perfect counter against them. She didn't want to be a killer though, and ended up escaping to Gotham City, which had been ravaged by disease and an earthquake.

During this time, Huntress was dressing as Batman, creating rumors of a new Batgirl. Cass would end up taking up the costume after Huntress dropped it and joined the Bat-Family. Cass was trained by Barbara Gordon to be a hero, but everyone knew that she could waste Barbara even if she wasn't in the wheelchair at that point (and that's saying something, because Barbara as Oracle was known for destroying everyone who thought she was a pushover because she was paralyzed). Even Batman caught those hands. Well, "caught" is the wrong thing because it implies that he could do anything about it, which he can't. Cass is a better fighter even than the Dark Knight, making her one of the most potent martial artists of them all.

Spider-Man is Marvel's most relatable hero and quickly became one of the most popular superheroes ever. However, Spidey was a teen when he started, so he was a bit too young for a sidekick. Over the years, the Wall-Crawler would get partners, heroes who fought alongside him, but rarely ever had what would be considered his own sidekick. In the 2000s, he ended up joining the Avengers and becoming a more important hero than ever, which would eventually lead to him getting a sidekick, the teen known as Alpha.

Andy Maguire was at Horizon Labs and ended up in a lab accident that was similar to Peter's. However, instead of getting spider powers or something like that, he ended up gaining a measure of control over cosmic energies. Andy became Alpha and Spider-Man ended up working with the young hero, showing him the ropes. However, Alpha was never very popular with readers and has been fighting crime in Pittsburgh, far away from the center of the Marvel Universe.

What sidekicks do you do you think outclass their mentors? Do they look the part? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Ebenezer Was Johnny Depp’s Big Screen ‘Test’ (And Studios Barely Gave Him A Passing Grade)
articles.summary: Did Depp's Hollywood comeback work out?
articles.content:
Johnny Depp has had a long and wildly successful career as a character actor, spanning decades on TV and film. Over the last few years he's stepped away from Hollywood (and the United States) , seeking privacy following the verdict in his defamation trial against Amber Heard . His return to the industry came as the titular role in Ti West's Ebenzer , which arrived in theaters last weekend. This was reportedly a big test for the 63 year-old actor, and studios allegedly barely gave him a passing grade.

At the time of writing this story, Ebenzer has made $43.4 million on a reported budget of $38 million. Johnny Depp took a huge pay cut to keep at number low, but it wasn't enough to reach huge box office numbers of previous projects like the Pirates of the Caribbean movies . If this source is to be believed, the powers at Hollywood might not be inclined to give him major gigs following how Ti West's new movie did.

We should probably take these quotes with a grain of salt, but it should be interesting to see where/if Johnny Depp appears in another major film production. He returned to acting in Jeanne du Barry , but that was a French film produced outside of the Hollywood machine. While he's got plenty of beloved movies on his resume, it's unclear if moviegoing audiences can get past the Amber Heard ordeal and still want to show up in theaters to see him on the big screen.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Ridley Scott's Blade Runner is still one of the most influential sci-fi films of all time, and it has inspired an entire franchise of sequels that will continue with Amazon Prime Video's new series, Blade Runner 2099 . Set 80 years after the original film, the new series is set in a future where the artificial lifeforms known as Replicants have led a successful uprising and become the dominant race in Los Angeles, while humans have become second-class citizens.

Oscar-winner Michelle Yeoh ( Everything Everywhere All at Once ) stars in Blade Runner 2099 as Olwen, a Replicant Blade Runner who is nearing the end of her lifespan. Olwen partners with a human named Cora (Hunter Schafer), who is impersonating a replicant. The pair take on the case of hunting down a gang of rogue Replicants operating in the city, which quickly becomes a much deeper assignment than it initially seems (typical Blade Runner ).

ComicBook.com's Chris Killian had the chance to speak with Michelle Yeoh and the cast of Blade Runner 2099 at the press junket for the show. Even though Yeoh plays a character similar to Harrison Ford's Rick Deckard or (more specifically) Ryan Gosling's K from the sequel film, Blade Runner 2049 , she said it was Rutger Hauer's villain character from the original film, Roy Batty, who inspired her take on Olwen the most.

"I think all the replicants at the beginning, when you see Owen, she's very calm. She's come to accept. I'm dying in a few days. No big deal. You know, move on. Complete your mission. Get it done," Yeoh explained. "But I think there is always that moment, like. Why? Who decided that I should die? Should I go before I finish what I want to set up to do? I think a life lived well is… I've seen more than anyone else on the planet has seen. I've done more than anybody else could."

Blade Runner is one of the pioneering examples of the neo-noir subgenre. Ridley Scott took classic Film Noir tropes and married them to the sci-fi genre, much like he mixed sci-fi and horror to create Alien . As such, Blade Runner has a proud tradition of throwing a Noir twist into the story, and Michelle Yeoh teases that it could be the same with Olwen.

"So she's found a sense of contentment. But as the story goes on, you go like 'No, no, no, no, no.' There is something that she's holding back that we are not sure of. What is it? Why is she on this mission? Why is she not just spending the last couple of days having a glass of wine, chilling and all that, and going out and getting beaten up?

Blade Runner 2099 premieres on November 25th and will stream exclusively on Prime Video.

articles.title: The Next Bond Theme: From Taylor Swift to Raye, 16 Singers Who Could Croon for Robert Pattinson’s 007
articles.summary: The James Bond films are filled with traditions: the martinis are shaken, not stirred; the tuxes are immaculately tailored; the women are gorgeous; the villains are fascinating. Importantly, the films wouldn't be true Bond stories without a dramatic theme song written and performed by a star. Nancy Sinatra, Shirley Bassey, Paul McCartney & Wings, Madonna, […]
articles.content:
Many Bond numbers are heavy on brass and horns. Insert Marc Anthony, who can make any song feel cinematic. In 2024, Lin-Manuel Miranda penned an op-ed for Variety calling the 58-year-old the Latino community’s Frank Sinatra, writing: “He is our Sinatra and when we hear him, we also hear the echoes of all the unforgettable moments in our own lives.” The salsa king will have his “The Last Dance World Tour” in 2027, so perhaps he can fit in a nice writing credit to bring some excitement to the new iteration of 007? Let’s give him a sweeping bilingual ballad about loving someone who’s going to betray you, and the audience will melt in their seats. — C.D.

Bond can always use some Latin flavor! Who wouldn't be more iconic than the biggest artist on the planet? Bad Bunny already conquered the Super Bowl, and his album “DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOTOS” became the first fully Spanish-language album to win the Grammy for album of the year. The Puerto Rican superstar already has a bit of assassin experience with his scene-stealing turn in the film “Bullet Train.” Can you imagine a moody, reggaeton-laced theme in Spanish playing over the opening titles, followed by a revolutionary performance on the Oscars telecast? A global event, indeed. — C.D.

The Queen can do no wrong. Beyoncé already has some experience in the spy business, having played Foxxy Cleopatra in “Austin Powers in Goldmember.” Now it’s time for her to take on the real deal. Fresh off winning Album of the Year at the 2025 Grammys for “Cowboy Carter,” and with two Oscar-nominated songs to her credit— “Listen” from “Dreamgirls” and “Be Alive” from “King Richard” — expectations would be sky-high. A Tina Turner-inspired Bond theme, complete with powerhouse vocals and a rock-and-soul edge, could be the perfect way to usher in a new era of 007. — C.D.

Do we remember the Winter Olympics in Milan? That soaring high note on the Italian classic “Volare” reminded us that Mariah Carey still has it, and it’s almost criminal that she hasn’t conquered this kingdom yet. That five-octave range is tailor-made for an iconic Bond finale: the orchestra drops out, the tension builds, and Mariah unleashes one final, earth-shattering note on a slow-burning ballad. Give us Mariah! — C.D.

The Bond universe isn't averse to fresh blood when it comes to picking younger, newer artists for theme songs (see: Billie Eilish and Adele), so it's not entirely out of the realm of possibility that Olivia Dean could be tapped to record an original for the new Bond film. She's got the range and poise that live up to the most classic of Bond themes, plus her British pedigree suits her cleanly for the role. Put her in the studio with an orchestra and you've got yourself a formula for Bond magic. — S.H.

Few artists make more sense to record a Bond theme than Lana Del Rey, whose sweeping ballads and cinematic songwriting scream 007. And it would be something of a redemptive arc for her, considering that she previously revealed that she had penned and recorded the song "24" from her "Honeymoon” album for “Spectre," only for Sam Smith to get the job. Del Rey has since inched closer to Bond glory earlier this year with "First Light," the theme for the video game "007 First Light," but the big ticket is just out of reach. — S.H.

Earlier this year, Cynthia Erivo performed at the Hollywood Bowl and delivered a remarkable rendition of Gladys Knight's "Licence to Kill" from the James Bond film of the same name. Dear Denis Villeneuve and the Bond producers: you must watch the performance on YouTube and consider Erivo. She's perfectly British, and her vocals are elegant, soulful and filled with grandeur. She also has a cinematic style and would be a perfect entry into the Bond franchise. — J.T.

The Canadian chanteuse is back in the public eye after struggling with health issues, and who better to deliver a soaring anthem that unites the world? She's no stranger to the genre, delivering gems such as the indelible "My Heart Will Go On" for "Titanic" and the underrated "Ashes" for "Deadpool 2." Plus her powerful four octave range is sure to match the intensity of any orchestra she's singing alongside. Step aside and let Dion put the "power" in "power ballad." — W.E.

Lady Gaga knows how to write music for film. She won an Oscar for “Shallow" from "A Star Is Born," and she wrote “Harlequin,” an album inspired by her “Joker: Folie à Deux” character Harley Quinn. This week, she landed two Grammy nominations for “Runway,” from “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” She also has the vocal range to deliver jazz standards, as displayed during her Las Vegas Residency, “Jazz and Piano.” Gaga checks the boxes to write a soaring classic 007 theme. — J.T.

Raye, who was recently named Variety ’s 2026 Hitmaker of the Year, is one of music's hottest stars. And yet her voice has a timeless quality which would certainly speak to old-school Bond fans who are looking for a more classically-sounding theme. Plus, her smoky vocals can stand alongside complex arringements, which come with the territory on Bond songs. Plus, she has the secret agent bona fides down, as she's best known for solving a mystery … after all, where the hell is her husband? — W.E.

We already have a James Bond theme song preview from Rosalía if anyone has listened to “Lux,” her fourth studio album, where she sings in 13 languages, paired with operatic vocals and a thundering choice with Björk. The Spanish-born pop star is incredibly hot at the moment, as shown by pulling in nine Grammy nominations this year and a résumé that includes 13 number-one hits. She can bring the drama, the intrigue and a little flamenco flair to the next 007 adventure. — C.D.

She’s not quite the superstar, yet, that virtually all the others on this list are, but she’s certainly on or approaching that bubble. That the British upstart styles herself like someone right out of a ’60s swinging-London film helps set the mood for thinking of her as a Bond girl: You could visually picture her silhouette fitting right into the title sequence, without having to hire a ringer. But it’s not so much about her nostalgic look — it’s that voice, which one of her obvious inspirations, former Bond theme-stress Adele, has cosigned. The most obvious sign it could or should be Spiro: one great song on her new album, called “Time, You and Me,” already sounds like a classic Bond theme. If it were, it’d be one of the two or three best 007 songs this century. Spiro could surely find another one where that came from. — C.W.

Harry Styles would be the perfect candidate to write the new James Bond theme. Having gone from One Direction breakout to a hugely successful solo performer, Styles can deliver both pop and rock with strong vocals. He also co-wrote the Bleachers song “Alfie's Song (Not So Typical Love Song)” for the 2018 film "Love, Simon," but that was more of a pop bop. Think instead of 2017’s “Sign of the Times.” The song is a perfect power ballad. For Bond, Styles would be matched with a large orchestra. And despite a screen test, if he can't get to play James Bond, delivering a Bond song for the franchise would be the next best thing. — J.T.

Hiring an A-list Bond? Consider an A-list superstar to do the theme. Swift is certainly ambitious enough to consider doing a 007 song, an elite club of music's best and brightest. She's certainly open to writing for films, as her current hit "I Knew It, I Knew You" is from "Toy Story 5" — and she's already hitting the promotional trail to ensure it gets ample Oscar consideration. But we know she could have an interesting take on the drama, intrigue and romance that fuels every Bond song … after all, her catalogue is filled with big emotions. — W.E.

Sure, there's novelty in getting Pattinson's longtime fiancée in the mix to sing his theme song. But Waterhouse is a respected musician with three albums and plenty of touring under her belt, and a sultry alto that adds texture to her indie rock hits. Her most recent album, "Loveland" has some complex arrangements, and she's still able to hold her own, which is necessary as the inevitable Bond theme orchestra swells. Hell, while we're at it, make her a Bond Girl, too, and tickets will sell like crazy. — W.E.

The Paramore belter has shown, between her band's genre experimentation and her own freewheeling solo material, that she's not constrained by sound. Although 007-style bombast would be yet another gear, it'd be fascinating for to try that style on for size. Besides, the Villeneuve Bond will inevitably be edgy: Williams is the perfect choice to bring some grit to the secret agent glam. Besides, Pattinson ushered in an era of the emo Batman … could an emo Bond be next? If so, who better than Williams to sing his feelings! — W.E.

articles.title: Jared Padalecki And Leighton Meester Bonded Over Gossip Girl And Gilmore Girls In A G-Oriented Way I Didn't See Coming
articles.summary: I love this for them.
articles.content:
